The briefing as three pages

Brief 108, round 2 · Glyph · 2026-11-11 · design only, 1920×1080 frames · words are placeholders for Fable

Sky: "Should just explain little about the mission, first page; then second would be area of interest and third would be look out for. Doesn't need to cram onto one page for an intro mission." So the briefing is three calm pages with one idea each, then Begin. Every page has Back, a 1 · 2 · 3 indicator and Next. The dots are clickable too, so any page is one click away. The arrow keys ← → work as an extra, and Esc still opens the pause menu.

What each page holds

PageOn itHow it moves
1 · The missionPopovic's portrait, "Take Popovic alive" and three short story lines: who he is, why we want him, what we do. About 40 words.No Back on this page. Next goes to page 2.
2 · Where it happensFour places: our car, Inez's café, the front door and the pickup. Each has one line. The two ways in are places, so their rows carry a chip: "Way in · before 5:30" and "Way in · from 5:50". A click on a chip opens that way's steps, as in round 1's A2. The Journal follows them in play.The page slides right so the street has room. The camera visits each place once (about 3 s each), and the row being shown lights up while a label pins the place in the street. A click on a row sends the camera there and stops the tour.
3 · Look out forThe guard on the door, the cameras, the other crew (with its 2:35 time), the patrol robot and the police. Each has one line. This replaces "What can go wrong".Hovering a row pins that thing in the street, or turns the camera to it if it's off screen. Begin takes Next's place.

The patrol robot was checked: it is on this block. It walks the service yard on the Office's east face, behind the building. It moved there in brief 067; see GDD §07 places and the mission's patrol points. The guard, the cameras, the rivals and the robot each wear the marker the player will see over them in the street (the kit's badges). The police get the siren icon instead, because their in-game shield is too close to the guard's.

Skip to Begin: my choice

A quiet "Skip to Begin ›" on page 1, where Back would sit, shown only after the first play (a restart after a loss, or a new game). A first-time player always gets the three pages, because that's the introduction Sky asked for. A returning player shouldn't have to click through it again on every retry. It's a text link, not a button, so Next stays the obvious path. Page 1 still shows first, so each run opens on the story. The dots already let anyone jump to page 3.

What leaves the briefing

  • Money and Heat: gone. The HUD shows the cash in play, and Heat is zero on the first mission.
  • The nine ways to fail: gone. Page 3 covers the dangers, and the end card says what went wrong.
  • The checklists: behind the way chips, and in the Journal.
  • The five-stop timeline: the rivals' 2:35 is on page 3, and the 5:30 and 5:50 are on the way chips. The chime is already the HUD's next-event line.
  • The cell strip: the Cell tab.

Kept on every page: the weather pill and the clock at the top right, the folded "Dial DEV" chip at the bottom left of the street (it opens today's panel), and the tabs (Cell, Job, Menu).

Open for Sky

  • Is "Skip to Begin" only after the first play right, or should it never appear?
  • Page 2's tour: should it run once on arrival (my choice), or wait for clicks?

Mocks only. The streets are play captures from brief 103 (a little leftover HUD remains), and the faces are crops from the 063 concepts. The words are placeholders for Fable. Next: Sky rules, Fable writes the words, Latch builds (a page index on the Job section; each page a BookLayout; page 2's tour uses the turn the faces already do; the curve's edge animates between pages), then Glyph does the 2× crop check.
